guides.favoredWhen: Deny early farm with a bounced wave and freeze. Her ranged and later attack spikes make an even lane less attractive than an early experience lead.

keyTips.text: Freeze after pushing the first waves to bounce back. A frozen wave near your turret forces Kayle to walk up for every minion and gives you a long lane to run her down.
After level 6, threaten a committed all-in rather than trading your entire burst into Divine Judgment. Save damage or disengage during the invulnerability, then punish its cooldown.
Build your lead before level 11. Kayle becomes ranged at level 6, then gains stronger attack pressure at level 11; do not treat the earlier ranged spike as harmless.

tips.text: Deny early farm with a bounced wave and freeze. Her ranged and later attack spikes make an even lane less attractive than an early experience lead.
At level 1, use a delayed third Broken Wings cast to remove Bone Plating before committing. Kayle can win sustained attack trades while your Q is down, so wait for the next rotation.
Threaten trades that force Celestial Blessing. Each cast spends mana on healing and movement speed; repeated defensive casts leave Kayle fewer resources for farming and escaping your next engage.
Shield her empowered Starfire Spellblade auto and Radiant Blast with Valor when you walk up. Do not give her free poke while you set the freeze.
Trade ultimates when doing so leaves you safe: at equal ability haste, Blade of the Exile ({cd:92:R}) returns before Divine Judgment ({cd:10:R}). Check her haste before relying on that gap.
Ghost can replace Ignite if you need chase distance when Kayle pokes near your turret. Run her down along the long lane, while still saving damage for after Divine Judgment.
Punish Kayle whenever she steps into reach of your freeze. If she stays back, deny the minions instead of needlessly pushing the wave toward the safety of her turret.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and a Health Potion to sustain through Radiant Blast and attack poke while maintaining a freeze. Preserving health lets you punish her walk-ups without giving away an extended attack trade.

guides.favoredWhen: Interrupt Decimating Smash and deny early farm, while respecting its shortened recovery after interruption. Kill location matters because Glory in Death can recover a wave.

keyTips.text: Cancel Decimating Smash with Ki Burst or the third Broken Wings cast, but save a dash afterward. An interrupted charge receives a reduced cooldown, so it can return sooner than {cd:14:Q}.
Freeze near your turret and zone Sion from early minions. Forcing him to farm with Roar of the Slayer spends his mana while denying him easy attacks on the wave.
Time kills around his death passive. Do not kill him where Glory in Death can farm the whole wave and undo your denial.

tips.text: Interrupt Decimating Smash and deny early farm, while respecting its shortened recovery after interruption. Kill location matters because Glory in Death can recover a wave.
Trade hard at level 1 before Sion has accumulated much Soul Furnace health. Do not assume he learned its shield first; answer whichever spell he reveals.
Crash the third wave, recall, then freeze near your turret and bully every walk-up. He must expose himself to Decimating Smash the wave or lose farm.
If Roar of the Slayer hits you, leave Decimating Smash range immediately. The slow makes a charged hit easier to land, but does not guarantee it if you preserve a dash.
Build a lead before Soul Furnace health and armor make Sion too durable. Once kills become unrealistic, keep your farm instead of forcing burst into his shield.
Respect unwarded lane brush: Sion can charge Decimating Smash unseen. Approach with a dash available rather than walking into the release while farming.
When Soul Furnace is active, either break the shield with damage before it detonates or leave its blast range. Keep Valor for Decimating Smash rather than spending every dash on the shield.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for early denial. Black Cleaver adds health, haste and armor shred against his tank purchases; repeated physical hits apply it, while a fresh Soul Furnace shield still needs a deliberate response.

guides.favoredWhen: Counter Strike is the main commitment check. Build early advantages from its recovery windows and keep an escape available for Leap Strike.

keyTips.text: Bait Counter Strike before committing to an all-in ({cd:24:E}). During the dodge, your Runic Blade attacks will not land; preserve mobility to leave before its stun.
When Jax uses Leap Strike, shield the landing with Valor and use Ki Burst while moving away. Leave Counter Strike's area before it releases; shielding does not prevent its stun.
Keep Valor ready whenever you walk up to farm against Leap Strike and Counter Strike. Spending it for a minion can leave you unable to escape his next jump.

tips.text: Counter Strike is the main commitment check. Build early advantages from its recovery windows and keep an escape available for Leap Strike.
At level 1, avoid committing while Counter Strike is ready. If he spends it without catching you, use your next Broken Wings rotation before his dodge returns.
If you both reach level 2 together after starting Broken Wings, take Valor second. You need the shield for his Leap Strike plus Empower trade, not more damage.
From level 3, lead with Broken Wings, auto, Ki Burst, auto, then disengage. Stop there; extended autos let Relentless Assault stack against you.
Delay Broken Wings recasts, use the third cast to draw Counter Strike, then Ki Burst and retreat. With Broken Wings already recovering, your next rotation can arrive before Counter Strike.
Disengage from an activated Grandmaster-at-Arms unless you can finish Jax. Its gained resistances blunt your physical burst; wait for that defense to end before spending Wind Slash.
Keep the wave near your turret and build an early advantage from Counter Strike windows. Jax becomes harder to duel as he completes items, so turn safe trades into denied farm.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for early pressure, then consider Plated Steelcaps against physical attacks. Jax also deals magic damage with Empower, so armor is not permission to ignore Counter Strike.

guides.favoredWhen: Ionian Fervor stacks and nearby Bladesurge resets determine safe trades. Thin incoming waves and preserve a dash for Flawless Duet.

keyTips.text: Trade while Ionian Fervor is low and check nearby low-health minions before engaging. If Bladesurge resets will let her finish stacking during your trade, leave instead of extending.
Save Valor or a Broken Wings cast for Flawless Duet. If its stun lands, prioritize escaping once it ends instead of extending into Ionian Fervor attacks.
Hold Wind Slash until Irelia cannot Bladesurge out of its path. Use Ki Burst to control her position before firing rather than aiming while a low-health minion offers her an escape.

tips.text: Ionian Fervor stacks and nearby Bladesurge resets determine safe trades. Thin incoming waves and preserve a dash for Flawless Duet.
Pressure level 1 if Irelia starts Flawless Duet, but do not overstay until Ionian Fervor stacks. Denying her early access to the wave is safer than an extended stacked fight.
When Irelia uses Bladesurge to last-hit a low-health minion with few passive stacks, Ki Burst her on arrival. The stun delays her next move; it does not remove the kill-based Bladesurge reset.
Freeze on your side after the incoming wave thins. Do not fight inside a large enemy push: dying allied minions give Irelia Bladesurge resets and Ionian Fervor stacks.
Wait for Defiant Dance to end before using Wind Slash or your main burst. Irelia reduces incoming physical damage during the channel, including Riven's ultimate damage.
During an all-in, aim Broken Wings through Irelia to change sides as she casts Vanguard's Edge. Do not run at her in a straight line with every dash already spent.
Respect Blade of the Ruined King as Irelia's first-item spike. Easier Bladesurge last-hits and stronger attack trades mean you must reassess her available resets before dueling.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade for pressure or Doran's Shield against repeated poke, with a Health Potion. Plated Steelcaps reduce physical attack damage, but Ionian Fervor also adds magic damage, so the boots do not neutralize full stacks.

guides.favoredWhen: Preserve health through Parrrley poke and contest Powder Kegs. Level 6 improves your burst threat, provided barrels and early armor do not stop your approach.

keyTips.text: Shield Parrrley with Valor rather than taking repeated poke. When Valor is down ({cd:92:E}), concede a last-hit if collecting it would expose you to another free shot.
Auto his Powder Kegs whenever you trade near one. Killing a keg denies its damage and the speed he gains from detonating it.
At level 6, remove Bone Plating before committing Blade of the Exile. Your burst threat improves, but Cannon Barrage still damages and slows you during the chase.

tips.text: Preserve health through Parrrley poke and contest Powder Kegs. Level 6 improves your burst threat, provided barrels and early armor do not stop your approach.
Start Valor at level 1 with Doran's Shield if he pokes with Parrrley; if he starts Powder Keg instead, start Broken Wings and contest the keg before it arms.
Avoid fighting beside brush you have not checked. Gangplank can hide a Powder Keg there and connect another keg to hit you before you reach him.
Track his available kegs under his health bar. Trade when the count is low and he must replace a keg before he can threaten a chain.
A Sheen-first Gangplank can be vulnerable to level-6 burst before buying armor. Ki Burst him beside a nearly depleted Powder Keg, destroy the keg, then continue the all-in.
If you chunk him and the wave pushes toward him, threaten a dive with your jungler rather than letting him farm safely under turret with oranges and kegs.
With ability haste, delay Broken Wings recasts and punish Gangplank when he steps too close. Spend fewer dashes reaching him so more casts and Runic Blade attacks hit him.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and a Health Potion to preserve health against Parrrley. Plated Steelcaps can reduce attack damage and add armor against Powder Keg's physical damage, but do not replace destroying kegs.

guides.favoredWhen: Early pressure and mana preservation offer openings before armor stacks. Once Plated Steelcaps blunt your damage, farming and roaming are often more productive.

keyTips.text: Disengage the moment Ground Slam lands. Its attack-speed slow ruins your auto weaving, so dash out and wait for the slow to fade before trading again.
Absorb Seismic Shard with Valor and preserve health as Malphite spends mana. Look for a heavier trade once he lacks mana for Ground Slam ({cd:54:E}), rather than taking poke unshielded.
Pressure Malphite before his armor purchases. Once Plated Steelcaps make kills unlikely, favor farming and roaming instead of spending every rotation trying to break his defenses.

tips.text: Early pressure and mana preservation offer openings before armor stacks. Once Plated Steelcaps blunt your damage, farming and roaming are often more productive.
If Malphite starts Seismic Shard, punish after he spends it. If he holds Ground Slam, walk toward its range then step back to bait the cast before starting an attack trade.
From level 3, trade with an attack and Ki Burst, then Valor out before Ground Slam can punish your follow-up. Do not keep attacking while its attack-speed reduction is on you.
Against Arcane Comet poke, use Doran's Shield and Second Wind to preserve health while he spends mana. Avoid letting each Seismic Shard force an unshielded last-hit attempt.
At level 6, look for burst after lowering Malphite toward sixty percent health, provided armor has not already made him too durable. Do not assume Wind Slash kills through Granite Shield.
Bait Thunderclap by threatening a close trade, then retreat after Ki Burst and an attack. Avoid standing still for his empowered attacks while your mobility is spent.
Keep Flash available for Unstoppable Force when committing at level 6. Valor can absorb damage, but its shield cannot prevent the knockup that gives Malphite time to finish you.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and a Health Potion against Seismic Shard poke. Build Black Cleaver into meaningful armor: its physical-damage shred, health and haste support repeated trades, but do not guarantee a kill on a tank build.
Mercury's Treads are an option against a poke-heavy magic-damage build. Magic resist helps against Seismic Shard and Ground Slam; tenacity does not shorten Unstoppable Force's knockup.

guides.favoredWhen: Fury and Ruthless Predator decide whether you can approach. Preserve health, deny safe Fury generation and punish Slice and Dice recovery.

keyTips.text: Stay outside Ruthless Predator range when Renekton has at least 50 Fury. Its empowered hit destroys Valor's shield before dealing damage, so shielding in place is not protection.
Control the wave to limit Renekton's safe attacks on minions. Denying that access slows his Fury generation before the next Ruthless Predator trade.
Shield Cull the Meek with Valor and take Bone Plating in runes against Ruthless Predator. Surviving his first rotation is what creates your trade back.

tips.text: Fury and Ruthless Predator decide whether you can approach. Preserve health, deny safe Fury generation and punish Slice and Dice recovery.
Cheese level 1 only before he gains experience and Fury, and only if he started Cull the Meek. If he started Ruthless Predator, respect the stun and farm.
Take brief trades with a minion advantage, but do not treat the wave as a shield. Slice and Dice passes through units, and hitting a unit enables his second dash.
Below half health Renekton generates Fury faster. Check his bar again before the next trade instead of assuming chip damage has made an empowered Ruthless Predator less likely.

At level 6, consider an Ignite all-in after Renekton wastes Ruthless Predator ({cd:58:W}) or Cull the Meek ({cd:58:Q}). Check his Fury, health and Dominus before committing; one spent spell is no guarantee.
Abuse Slice and Dice cooldown ({cd:58:E}) after he dashes in and out. Chase that window instead of trading while both dashes are ready.
After a short trade, leave enough distance that Slice and Dice cannot immediately punish the exit. Do not spend every dash beside a Renekton who still has a second dash ready.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion with Bone Plating to survive early burst. Plated Steelcaps add armor against his physical damage; they do not stop empowered Ruthless Predator from breaking Valor's shield.

Black Cleaver is an option into armor for health, haste and physical-damage shred. Death's Dance is a defensive first-item alternative when surviving Renekton's burst matters more than snowballing damage.

guides.favoredWhen: Wave control matters more than aimless poke. Deny Siphoning Strike stacks early and reassess once Fury of the Sands and armor arrive.

keyTips.text: Freeze to deny Siphoning Strike last-hits and delay Nasus's stacking. Repeatedly pushing into his turret instead gives him safer access to minions and Soul Eater healing.
During Wither, rely more on ability damage and movement than an extended attack trade. The attack-speed reduction weakens your autos; disengage instead of standing beside repeated Siphoning Strikes.
Treat level 6 and early armor as a reassessment point. A stack-starved Nasus remains punishable, but even farm and Fury of the Sands can remove the easy all-ins you had earlier.

tips.text: Wave control matters more than aimless poke. Deny Siphoning Strike stacks early and reassess once Fury of the Sands and armor arrive.
Assert level 1 by walking up and forcing Spirit Fire just to last-hit. Trading his mana for denied Siphoning Strike stacks wins you the lane slowly.
Preserve a freeze by avoiding unnecessary attacks on minions. Aim Broken Wings away from the wave when trading, since its area damage can push Nasus back toward safe stacking.
Punish every walk-up for a stack with Ki Burst and a short rotation, then return to the freeze instead of chasing him under his turret.
If you have already chunked Nasus, crash a wave for a coordinated early jungle dive. If he stays healthy, let the wave bounce and freeze instead of repeatedly pushing into Soul Eater sustain.
Do not absorb Spirit Fire's initial hit while maintaining the freeze. Let its damage help push his wave toward you rather than standing in it to force a trade.
After level 6, draw out Fury of the Sands and disengage if you cannot burst Nasus. Re-engage after it ends; avoid trading substantial health that Soul Eater will let him recover.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion to punish Siphoning Strike attempts. Consider Executioner's Calling when Soul Eater healing during combat matters, but brief Wounds will not cover every minion he attacks after you disengage.

guides.favoredWhen: Dodge Obliterate and keep trades below Darkness Rise activation. A charged Indestructible shield or an extended realm duel can absorb your burst.

keyTips.text: Finish your short trade before Mordekaiser lands three attacks or abilities and activates Darkness Rise. Leave the aura instead of taking an extended exchange inside it.
Keep Blade of the Exile available for a Realm of Death duel when possible. Do not fire Wind Slash during his transition into the realm; wait until you are inside and can hit him.
Trade where Obliterate will also hit a minion. Its isolated-hit bonus applies when it strikes only one enemy, so a shared hit deals less damage to you.

tips.text: Dodge Obliterate and keep trades below Darkness Rise activation. A charged Indestructible shield or an extended realm duel can absorb your burst.
If you do not get a clean level-1 opening, wait for level 3 rather than fighting into Darkness Rise. Dodge Obliterate and avoid letting attacks complete his three-hit activation.
Sidestep Obliterate with a step, then Broken Wings, then Valor if needed. Jump behind him with Broken Wings so Death's Grasp pulls air.
Never all-in while Indestructible is fully charged. Trade once to force the shield and heal, leave, then commit before the bar refills.
At level 6, look for a Blade of the Exile all-in around half health after Indestructible is spent. A charged shield can absorb the burst you need to finish him.
If Mordekaiser uses Realm of Death without killing you, watch its recovery ({cd:82:R}). With the realm unavailable, he cannot isolate you on the next engage.
After dodging Death's Grasp ({cd:82:E}), trade briefly and leave before Darkness Rise activates. The missed pull buys room to disengage; it does not turn off an aura that is already active.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for damage in brief trades before Darkness Rise activates. Boots are an optional early purchase if movement speed helps you sidestep Obliterate without spending Valor.

guides.favoredWhen: Shield Decisive Strike, kite Judgment and draw Courage before the all-in. Good disengages matter more than spending every cast in melee range.

keyTips.text: Use Valor as Decisive Strike reaches you, adding Ki Burst before contact if you can. The shield absorbs damage; it does not prevent the silence, so prepare your exit beforehand.
Only all-in while Courage is down ({cd:86:W}). Its damage reduction eats Wind Slash, so bait it with one trade and burst on the next.
When Decisive Strike is down ({cd:86:Q}), take one Broken Wings rotation and leave. Avoid staying in melee range with every spell spent when his silence returns.

tips.text: Shield Decisive Strike, kite Judgment and draw Courage before the all-in. Good disengages matter more than spending every cast in melee range.
Freeze near your turret from the start and punish his walk-ups. He must enter your rotation to farm, and a short lane protects you from Judgment chase.
When he runs at you with Decisive Strike, meet him with your third Broken Wings cast at its edge to knock him up before the silence lands.
At level 1, bait Garen's learned spell with a delayed third Broken Wings cast. Re-engage on your next rotation only if he stays close while that spell is down.
If Judgment is already spinning, kite away after shielding Decisive Strike. Minions do not split its damage; the nearest enemy takes extra damage.
Respect Garen's Stridebreaker purchase. Its slow makes disengaging from Judgment harder, so preserve mobility instead of repeating the same close trades you took before the item.
Do not let Perseverance erase your lane pressure for free. Resume safe poke when your spells return, but avoid chasing into Decisive Strike and Judgment with no exit.

itemization.text: Start Long Sword and Refillable Potion for damage and repeat lane sustain. Use the damage in short trades around Decisive Strike, while preserving potion charges for repeated lane returns.

guides.favoredWhen: Respect empowered Twilight Assault attacks and Spirit's Refuge. After level 6, make Stand United cost him waves or interrupt the channel.

keyTips.text: Avoid spending Runic Blade attacks into Spirit's Refuge. Use Ki Burst if you need to stall him, then resume attacks only after the blocking zone ends.
Interrupt Stand United with Ki Burst or your third Broken Wings cast whenever he channels in reach, and chase him when he walks away to find an ultimate angle.
Track Shen's spirit blade before trading. If Twilight Assault misses its pull-through and Ki Barrier has expired, he has less protection for your next exchange.

tips.text: Respect empowered Twilight Assault attacks and Spirit's Refuge. After level 6, make Stand United cost him waves or interrupt the channel.
At level 1, draw Twilight Assault to trigger Ki Barrier and remove Bone Plating with a delayed third Broken Wings cast. Wait for those defenses to expire before committing to attacks.
Do not let the returning spirit blade pass through you during Twilight Assault. That collision strengthens Shen's next attacks; if it happens, leave their range rather than fighting into them.
Dodge Shadow Dash with a saved dash. If it connects, Ki Burst and leave when the taunt ends instead of staying beside empowered Twilight Assault attacks.
After level 6, keep a wave pushing into Shen before fights elsewhere when you can do so safely. Stand United then costs him minions and turret damage instead of giving him a free departure.
Avoid trading beneath Shen's turret with Shadow Dash ready. The taunt can force an attack on him and draw turret aggression even if you intended to leave after a short trade.

Once Shen has spent Spirit's Refuge and his empowered Twilight Assault attacks, you can extend an exchange if your health and spells allow it. Avoid letting him win through his initial burst, then leaving before your remaining damage lands.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for damage when Twilight Assault protection is spent. Item damage cannot make Runic Blade attacks connect through Spirit's Refuge, so preserve those attacks until it ends.

guides.favoredWhen: Avoid Frenzied Maul recasts and Sky Splitter shield trades. A cancelled Thundering Smash charge is not a spent stun, so choose re-engages carefully.

keyTips.text: Never trade while his Frenzied Maul mark is on you. Its recast heals him and deals bonus damage, so leave until the mark expires.
Bait Thundering Smash by walking close, then dash away. Stunning Volibear during the charge resets its cooldown, so Ki Burst alone does not create a Q-down trading window.
Use the level-1 opening to pressure Volibear before his stronger levels 2 and 3. Back off as he gains access to Thundering Smash and Sky Splitter together.

tips.text: Avoid Frenzied Maul recasts and Sky Splitter shield trades. A cancelled Thundering Smash charge is not a spent stun, so choose re-engages carefully.
Use only Ki Burst, an auto, then an instant dash out while Thundering Smash is ready. Longer casts let him stun you and layer Frenzied Maul on top.
After Volibear actually spends Thundering Smash ({cd:106:Q}), use a fuller Broken Wings trade if you are unmarked. Do not confuse an interrupted charge with a spent stun.
Bait Sky Splitter ({cd:106:E}) with brief contact and leave its circle. Re-engage after any shield expires so Volibear does not receive both free damage and protection.
Around half health, look for Blade of the Exile burst while Sky Splitter or Thundering Smash is spent and you are unmarked. A Frenzied Maul recast can still overturn the attempt.
If you stay even, aim for your second-item dueling spike instead of forcing level-2 or level-3 kills. Avoid giving Frenzied Maul repeat heals just to create an early lead.
Use a dash or Flash to avoid Stormbringer's central landing damage when necessary. Escaping that burst can matter more than saving Flash for a later engage.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and a Health Potion to preserve health through early pressure. Executioner's Calling is optional against Frenzied Maul healing, but avoiding the marked recast is still better than accepting it with Wounds applied.

guides.favoredWhen: Vital positioning and Riposte decide the lane. Riven can threaten early burst, but a recovery kill makes Fiora's later dueling much harder to contain.

keyTips.text: Draw out Riposte before committing Ki Burst or Wind Slash ({cd:114:W}). Its parry can deny your burst, and its return thrust slows attacks even without a stun.
Hold Valor when you use your third Broken Wings cast on her. She can read that cast for Riposte, so dash sideways after it to leave its line.
Hug a wall when Grand Challenge marks you. Denying access to one Vital makes it harder for Fiora to trigger the complete four-Vital heal.

tips.text: Vital positioning and Riposte decide the lane. Riven can threaten early burst, but a recovery kill makes Fiora's later dueling much harder to contain.
Play level 1 close to your minions and punish a missed Lunge. A miss gets no hit-based cooldown refund ({cd:114:Q}); check that she did not hit another unit.
Walk out of her vision to move your Vital to a worse spot for her. Do not offer a front Vital she can Lunge onto for free.
Freeze near your turret after letting her shove first. A long lane punishes Riposte waste, and your turret covers trades she tries to extend.
At level 6, all-in a chipped Fiora when Riposte is spent. If your third Broken Wings cast lands, follow promptly with Ki Burst rather than leaving a gap for her parry.
Disengage if Riposte hits you and your burst is no longer lethal. Its attack-speed reduction weakens Runic Blade attacks even when the thrust only slows you.
Keep a lead safe rather than giving Fiora a recovery kill. Her Vital damage and Grand Challenge make later side-lane duels dangerous even after you win lane.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for early trading. Consider Executioner's Calling when Vital healing matters during fights, and Plated Steelcaps against her physical attacks; armor does not reduce Vital true damage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wants a long lane and enough time to stack Hemorrhage. Keep exchanges short until his health and Apprehend cooldown permit a fast kill.

keyTips.text: Never finish Broken Wings with its third cast while Apprehend is ready. A good Darius holds it to cancel that cast instead of using it to start the trade.
Move inside Decimate or dash through it. The inner handle does far less and does not heal him like the blade edge does.
Leave before Hemorrhage reaches five stacks. Do not start another exchange with bleed stacks still on you; wait for them to expire before re-engaging.

tips.text: Darius wants a long lane and enough time to stack Hemorrhage. Keep exchanges short until his health and Apprehend cooldown permit a fast kill.
Consider a level-1 all-in if Darius starts Decimate and you can avoid its blade edge. This is a conditional opening, not permission to duel every Darius start or summoner setup.
Trade when he last-hits or misses Apprehend ({cd:122:E}): Ki Burst, auto, then Valor plus Broken Wings out before Hemorrhage builds.
Let him push and freeze near your turret when he has Ghost. A short lane near your turret denies the long run-down where Ghost and bleed kill you.
At level 6, look for a Blade of the Exile all-in after short trades lower him toward half health and Apprehend is spent. Armor purchases can push that kill threshold lower.
Before ability haste items, never spend every cast to engage far from safety. With everything down, Darius walks you down even after a good first trade.
If Darius has Ghost and Ignite, require a missed Apprehend before committing far from safety. Teleport replaces one combat summoner and reduces that run-down threat.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for short trades. Ignite helps finish a chipped Darius and reduces Decimate healing if its blade connects during the all-in.

guides.favoredWhen: Preserve health against Shock Blast before level 6. Bait Thundering Blow or use the brief transform lockout to reach him with your ultimate available.

keyTips.text: Look to engage just after Jayce changes from hammer to cannon form. His transform must recover before he can return to Thundering Blow; the opening is brief, not the whole cannon stance.
Before level 6, only last-hit when Valor or a Broken Wings cast is ready to dodge Shock Blast. Farming without a dash ready costs too much health.
At level 6, bait Thundering Blow before committing Blade of the Exile. Your new ultimate adds burst, while Jayce still relies on his existing hammer and cannon spells.

tips.text: Preserve health against Shock Blast before level 6. Bait Thundering Blow or use the brief transform lockout to reach him with your ultimate available.
Let him push into you and farm under your side of lane. A pushed Jayce is exposed to ganks and cannot poke you off every minion from range.
If he jumps on you with To the Skies!, Ki Burst him on landing and trade briefly, then leave before Thundering Blow knocks you into his cannon swap.
Cheese at level 1 only when he lacks Phase Rush or facechecks brush. Otherwise respect cannon poke and preserve health for level 6.
Respect Jayce's early lethality purchases, such as Serrated Dirk. Their armor penetration makes physical poke more punishing, so preserve health instead of assuming a level-6 all-in is automatic.
Build ability haste to make delayed Broken Wings trades more frequent. Re-engage when Thundering Blow is actually spent; changing form alone does not consume the knockback cooldown.
During an all-in, hold the third Broken Wings cast while Jayce is in hammer form with Thundering Blow ready. He can cancel your knockup with his knockback.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and a Health Potion with Second Wind against cannon poke. Preserving health for level 6 gives more useful all-in chances than losing the lane to repeated Shock Blast casts.

sources.author: Saltyy
sources.rankClaim: Former Diamond player, currently unranked; 2M+ Riven mastery (site info page, self-claim) - Riven main

guides.favoredWhen: Camille trades around Adaptive Defenses and Hookshot. Spending those defenses first opens a stronger level-6 all-in for Riven.

keyTips.text: Spend Adaptive Defenses before committing damage. Let her attack into Valor, wait for the shield to expire, and remove Bone Plating before the next trade.

Interrupt Hookshot with Ki Burst or the third Broken Wings cast as the hook attaches and Camille moves toward the wall. Once both dash parts are spent, use its recovery window ({cd:164:E}) for your next trade.
Stun her before Wind Slash. The Hextech Ultimatum can dodge Wind Slash, so Ki Burst first and only then fire it.

tips.text: Camille trades around Adaptive Defenses and Hookshot. Spending those defenses first opens a stronger level-6 all-in for Riven.
Play toward lane center while Hookshot is ready. Standing beside a wall gives Camille a shorter, harder-to-dodge Wall Dive into you.
Hold Valor for her engage and dodge Tactical Sweep with sideways Broken Wings casts. Eating the outer sweep heals her and slows you out of the trade.
Respect Camille's Trinity Force spike. Its Spellblade proc strengthens Precision Protocol's delayed recast, so do not judge that attack by its pre-item damage.
At level 6, all-in near sixty to seventy percent health when Hookshot is down ({cd:164:E}). If it is up, she escapes or turns the trade with a wall stun.
Check Camille's summoner spells. Against Ignite and Teleport, interrupting Hookshot removes her main escape because she has no Flash to cover the failed dash.
Use Valor or Broken Wings to leave attack range before the delayed Precision Protocol recast. Mobility can deny that hit; its true damage is not reduced by armor.

itemization.text: Start Long Sword and a Health Potion to put early gold into damage. Use that damage after Adaptive Defenses expires rather than trying to burst its fresh shield.

sources.author: Saltyy
sources.rankClaim: Former Diamond player, currently unranked; 2M+ Riven mastery (site info page, self-claim) - Riven main

guides.favoredWhen: Aatrox rewards missed dodges with healing. Preserve mobility for The Darkin Blade, then turn early cooldown gaps into a lead before armor blunts your burst.

keyTips.text: Keep trades brief before Conqueror fully stacks and strengthens Aatrox's sustained fighting. Do not stay beside him after your mobility is spent.
Use Broken Wings to move behind the first two casts of The Darkin Blade. Reserve a Broken Wings cast or Valor for disengaging so its third sweet spot does not catch your exit.
Do not commit Blade of the Exile into a full-health Aatrox. First lower him toward half health so your burst can finish before repeated healing.

tips.text: Aatrox rewards missed dodges with healing. Preserve mobility for The Darkin Blade, then turn early cooldown gaps into a lead before armor blunts your burst.
Do not walk into The Darkin Blade range with every dash spent. Aatrox can aim its sweet spots freely when you have neither Broken Wings nor Valor to reposition.

Bait Infernal Chains and Umbral Dash before committing. After the third cast of The Darkin Blade, punish its recovery window ({cd:266:Q}); without Umbral Dash he cannot reposition the next sweet spot.
Space out Broken Wings recasts rather than spending all three immediately. Keeping a dash available makes it harder for Aatrox to predict Valor with The Darkin Blade.
Respect Aatrox after Serrated Dirk: preserve health and farm rather than assuming the trades you won before his purchase still work.
If he rushes Plated Steelcaps, prioritize farm and turret plates over forcing kills. His armor reduces the physical damage of your attacks and abilities.
Get early push priority at level 1 while keeping close enough to move behind The Darkin Blade. Avoid casting Broken Wings in place inside a sweet spot.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion with Flash and Ignite for early pressure. Ignite reduces Aatrox's healing during the kill attempt.
Consider Executioner's Calling if repeated healing is preventing kills. Its Wounds apply while you deal physical damage; they do not permanently stop healing after you leave the trade.

sources.author: Saltyy
sources.rankClaim: Former Diamond player, currently unranked; 2M+ Riven mastery (site info page, self-claim) - Riven main

guides.favoredWhen: Avoid Bellows Breath's final hit and Searing Charge terrain setups. Early pressure is valuable before his armor makes repeated kill attempts wasteful.

keyTips.text: Dash through Ornn before Bellows Breath's final tick hits you. Avoiding that tick prevents its Brittle mark and the empowered attack that would consume it.
Stay away from walls and the Volcanic Rupture pillar while Searing Charge is ready. A collision there gives Ornn a knockup that your shield cannot prevent.
Save Ki Burst and the third Broken Wings knockup until Bellows Breath finishes. Ornn is unstoppable during the breath, so using crowd control then loses its interruption value.

tips.text: Avoid Bellows Breath's final hit and Searing Charge terrain setups. Early pressure is valuable before his armor makes repeated kill attempts wasteful.
Pressure at level 1 if Ornn did not learn Bellows Breath, after removing Bone Plating. Do not assume a free all-in into a ready breath and Brittle attack.
Remove Bone Plating, crash the third wave, recall, then freeze and bully every farm attempt. Away from his turret he must walk into your full rotation.
Use Valor to absorb damage from Ornn's Brittle attack if you cannot avoid it. The shield reduces damage taken, but does not prevent the mark from being consumed or its knockback.
Pressure Ornn before he purchases armor, including armor forged in lane with Living Forge. Once he is too durable, take farm instead of forcing repeated Brittle trades.
Keep Ki Burst or the third Broken Wings cast for Ornn's Call of the Forge God recast. Interrupt him before he redirects the ram to deny the returning knockup.
Trade immediately after Bellows Breath is spent ({cd:516:W}), provided Brittle is not still on you. Do not extend merely because the fire animation ended if he can still consume the mark.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for early pressure, or Doran's Shield if poke prevents trades. Black Cleaver supplies armor shred, health and haste once Ornn builds defenses; it does not prevent Brittle damage or knockups.

sources.author: Saltyy

guides.favoredWhen: Facebreaker and Haymaker make careless sustained trades dangerous. Use short exchanges with an escape ready instead of letting his stun set up a centered Haymaker.

keyTips.text: From level 3, bait Facebreaker before trading freely ({cd:875:E}). Spending the pull removes Sett's reliable early setup for a centered Haymaker.
Dash sideways or through Sett as Haymaker releases. Its center deals true damage, so retreating straight along that center line wastes your escape.
At a last-hit, use Ki Burst and one attack, then leave with Valor or Broken Wings available. Do not spend your whole rotation beside a ready Facebreaker.

tips.text: Facebreaker and Haymaker make careless sustained trades dangerous. Use short exchanges with an escape ready instead of letting his stun set up a centered Haymaker.
At level 1, remove his Bone Plating before any real trade, and only all-in if he started Haymaker and wasted it. Otherwise wait for level 3.
From level 3, bait Facebreaker at its edge, then trade with Ki Burst, an attack, and Valor plus Broken Wings away. Do not linger for Haymaker after forcing the pull.
Facebreaker only stuns if Sett catches enemies on both sides. Avoid a long fight with allied minions opposite you while his E and Haymaker are ready; that sets up a centered Haymaker.
At level 6, all-in near sixty percent health only while Haymaker is down ({cd:875:W}). If it is up, trade once to force it out, reset, then re-engage.
Expect Sett to reposition Haymaker with Flash. Preserve a mobility spell rather than assuming your first sidestep has already avoided its center.
If Facebreaker pulls without stunning you, Ki Burst and disengage. If it stuns, wait out the control and prioritize escaping Haymaker over finishing your damage.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion for short trades after Facebreaker is spent. Keep gold in damage for the later all-in; do not assume an early anti-heal purchase prevents Pit Grit regeneration between trades.

sources.author: Saltyy
sources.rankClaim: Former Diamond player, currently unranked; 2M+ Riven mastery (site info page, self-claim) - Riven main

guides.favoredWhen: Use the early damage advantage before Gwen's first item. Snip Snip! and Hallowed Mist windows are safer than a full-health sustained duel.

keyTips.text: Trade after Gwen spends Snip Snip! ({cd:887:Q}), especially a stacked cast on the wave. The window is brief because its cooldown falls with ranks.
Bait Hallowed Mist before the all-in. Gwen gains resistances inside it and is protected from enemies outside; wait out the mist rather than firing Wind Slash from outside it.
Never stand still for Needlework. Keep moving with Broken Wings casts between autos so each needle wave misses part of its damage.

tips.text: Use the early damage advantage before Gwen's first item. Snip Snip! and Hallowed Mist windows are safer than a full-health sustained duel.
If Gwen approaches the wave at level 1 without Snip Snip! stacks, look for an early all-in. Once she has stacked the snips, bait that cast before committing.
When Snip Snip! is fully stacked, stay beyond Skip 'n Slash plus Snip Snip! reach. Bait the snips on a last-hit and dash sideways instead of absorbing the center.
Against a Gwen with Ignite when you lack it, avoid gambling on a level-1 or level-2 all-in. Favor a short exchange and leave before her sustained damage takes over.

If Gwen spends Skip 'n Slash and Snip Snip! and ends beside you, attack without wasting Broken Wings to close distance. Her dash can partially refund on an attack, so do not assume its full cooldown is available.
Avoid a full-health all-in while even once Gwen has her first item. Chip her first; otherwise A Thousand Cuts healing and Needlework can extend the fight beyond your burst.
Respect Exhaust after Gwen reaches level 6. The damage reduction can stop your burst kill and give her time to hit successive Needlework casts; do not force a full-health all-in into both.

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and a Health Potion to pressure Gwen before her first item. Delay Executioner's Calling until after your first completed damage item if healing warrants it; do not delay early burst just to rush Wounds.

sources.author: Saltyy
sources.rankClaim: Former Diamond player, currently unranked; 2M+ Riven mastery (site info page, self-claim) - Riven main

keyTips.text: Build the early game around pressure and a favorable wave, not a forced all-in: slow-push by hitting the wave slightly more than the opponent to earn a level edge, a safer trade, and a crash that enables a recall, plates, or first move.
Weave basic attacks between Q recasts and delay the third Q until near the end of its recast window so the sequence returns sooner after the combo.
For a major objective, buy and push the opposite side lane roughly one to two minutes before it spawns, then move over with a flank route instead of walking down the river into vision.

tips.text: Trade when the opponent steps forward to last-hit, but weigh each exchange against losing your own minion; keep farming when the trade is not clearly worthwhile.
Track level-up timings at levels two, three, and six, holding the wave and Q timing so a new skill or the ultimate lands inside a prepared trade.
Take fights closer to your own side of the lane and stop the trade before it extends under the enemy turret.
Start Doran's Blade, Health Potion, and Stealth Ward, with Long Sword plus Refillable Potion or Pickaxe as the early purchase options.
Use Riven's mobility to keep collecting side-lane waves for solo experience and gold, then rotate the moment a fight or objective turns valuable.
Never share a side wave unnecessarily: when several opponents vanish to answer the push, retreat unless the fight is winnable, and return before the wave reaches your own turret.
Concede the objective rather than walking into a poor fight when the side lane cannot create pressure or a numbers edge; Teleport, vision, or a pick can change that call.
Enter teamfights from fog or a flank toward the backline or another high-value target, coordinating with allied engage or peel instead of charging a grouped team.
Choose fights on advantage: more champions present, key enemy abilities unavailable, and both sides' summoner spells accounted for.
Turn lane pressure from controlled waves and timed trades into side-lane experience, tower damage, or a flank at the next major objective.
Commit only on a favorable angle at a valuable target, then disengage or concede when enemy numbers and cooldowns make the fight poor.

itemization.text: Run Conqueror with Triumph, Legend: Haste, Last Stand, Cash Back, and Jack of All Trades for extended fights and ability hits, starting Flash and Ignite.

Build Axiom Arc into Endless Hunger and Death's Dance, then Lord Dominik's Regards, with a more defensive Death's Dance start when behind; max Q first, E second, and W last, taking R at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
